links.outcome: Physician accuracy, justification quality and confidence with vs without LLM assistance
links.effect: LLM assistance improved mean accuracy by 0.27±0.07 and justification quality by 10.45±1.96; gains consistent across fellows and consultants.
links.quote: LLM assistance improved mean accuracy by 0.27±0.07 and justification quality by 10.45±1.96.

links.outcome: Confidence-accuracy calibration (overconfidence) with LLM assistance by clinician experience
links.effect: Calibration improved for consultants (slope, -0.04 to 0.10) but declined for fellows (-0.17 to -0.40), indicating residual overconfidence among less experienced clinicians.
links.quote: Calibration improved for consultants (slope, -0.04 to 0.10) but declined for fellows (-0.17 to -0.40), indicating residual overconfidence among less experienced clinicians.

screen.reason: Evaluates physician diagnostic accuracy, justification quality, and confidence-accuracy calibration when using ChatGPT-4o as a clinical decision support tool on simulated clinical vignettes.

primary.practice: clinician use of LLM decision support
